name: LIPE-related Familial Partial Lipodystrophy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: LIPE-related Familial Partial Lipodystrophy Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of partial loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue predominantly affecting the limbs and trunk with relative preservation or accumulation in the face and neck
Identification of pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in the LIPE gene
Presence of metabolic complications including insulin resistance, diabetes mellitus, hypertriglyceridemia, and hepatic steatosis
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance of partial lipodystrophy
Clinical or imaging evidence of muscle pseudohypertrophy due to fat loss

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of partial lipodystrophy phenotype plus identification of a pathogenic LIPE variant and at least one metabolic abnormality
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis; clinical features may overlap with other lipodystrophies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Increased adipose tissue around the neck
Loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue in limbs
Loss of gluteal subcutaneous adipose tissue

common.symptomName: Proximal muscle weakness in lower limbs
Proximal muscle weakness in upper limbs

laboratory: Elevated fasting insulin and glucose levels indicating insulin resistance
Hypertriglyceridemia with triglyceride levels often >500 mg/dL
Elevated liver enzymes consistent with hepatic steatosis
imaging: MRI or CT demonstrating selective loss of subcutaneous fat in limbs and trunk
Ultrasound or MRI evidence of hepatic steatosis
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Generalized congenital absence of adipose tissue from birth
Severe insulin resistance presenting in infancy
Mutations in AGPAT2 or BSCL2 genes
Fat loss predominantly in limbs and trunk with accumulation in face and neck
Onset typically in adolescence or early adulthood

redFlags: Rapid onset of severe insulin resistance with partial fat loss
Severe hypertriglyceridemia refractory to standard treatment
Family history of similar fat distribution abnormalities and metabolic complications
references: Gandotra S, et al. Mutations in LIPE cause familial partial lipodystrophy. Am J Hum Genet. 2011;88(6): 845-851.
Moro C, et al. Clinical and genetic features of familial partial lipodystrophy. Nat Rev Endocrinol. 2020;16(3): 159-172.
